Use distance rank to summarize whether participants tend to recall closer available items next. It reads response files and a global item-distance matrix, then saves participant scores, a figure and uncertainty summaries.

Scores compare a chosen item’s distance with the alternatives available at that transition. The meaning of closeness comes from your distance matrix; this procedure does not establish that the matrix measures semantic similarity.

For input conventions, see the data guide.

Configure this run

Set distance_matrix_path to your item-distance matrix and select response files and conditions. distance_path is an optional compatibility override. Item IDs must refer to the same matrix rows in every dataset.

Choose participant-bootstrap settings for the reported uncertainty. Unlike distance-CRP, this analysis uses ranks of available distances and does not require distance bins.

Keep all editable settings in this tagged cell. Later cells derive paths and selections after any Papermill overrides.

1 — Set the parameters for this run 
# Inputs and saved results — change these for your project.
project_root = None  # Explicit folder, enclosing Git root, or current directory.
data_path = None  # A supplied single path takes precedence over data_paths.
data_paths = [
    "data/Dupertuys2026.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_CMR_demo_best_of_3.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_source_only_demo_best_of_3.h5",
    "data/simulations/Dupertuys2026_eCMR_broad_demo_best_of_3.h5",
]
data_labels = ["Observed", "CMR", "Source-only eCMR", "Broader eCMR"]
output_dir = "results/distrank"

# Observation selection — queries use fields in your dataset.
trial_query = None
trial_queries = ["data['list_type'] == 1"]
labels = ["Mixed lists"]
selection_label = "Mixed lists"
max_subjects = 0  # Zero keeps all participants; a positive value selects the first IDs.
complete_lists_only = False

# Scientific settings — choose these for the question you are asking.
distance_matrix_path = "data/Dupertuys2026_semantic_distances.npy"

# Uncertainty and optional behavioral summaries.
confidence_level = 0.95
plot_seed = 0  # Seed for bootstrap displays.
bootstrap_method = "BCa"
n_resamples = 9999
bootstrap_seed = 0

# Output overrides and appearance — None uses the default location or style.
figure_dir = None
figure_str = "distrank"  # Empty displays the figure without saving it.
figure_formats = ["png"]
contrast_name = None
color_cycle = None
ylim = None
yticks = None

# Optional input overrides and compatibility names.
distance_path = None  # Accept the earlier preview name when supplied.

Prepare the environment and inputs

Run the following setup cells once, then continue in order. The short installation cell runs only in Colab; local and Slurm runs use the environment you selected during Setup.

project_root anchors relative paths. When it is unset, Colab uses the current directory; elsewhere the notebook uses the enclosing Git project if present, or the current directory. Check the printed location. copy_example_inputs copies requested bundled examples there, reuses matching files, and refuses to overwrite conflicting files. Custom input paths remain your responsibility.

2 — Prepare the Colab environment 
import sys

if "google.colab" in sys.modules:

3 — Import packages 
import csv

import jax.numpy as jnp
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
from tabulate import tabulate

from jaxcmr.analyses.distrank import percentile_rank, plot_distrank, subject_distrank

from jaxcmr.dataset import _require_pres_itemids, select_conditions
from jaxcmr.examples import copy_example_inputs
from jaxcmr.helpers import load_data
from jaxcmr.helpers import resolve_project_path, resolve_project_root
from jaxcmr.plotting import save_figure
from jaxcmr.plotting import comparison_panels


from jaxcmr.analyses.statistics import compare_to_reference, mean_interval

Align items with the distance matrix

select_conditions returns the masks and participant coverage without altering your data. Check the printed list and participant counts before interpreting the results. Queries are Python expressions evaluated with the dataset named data; replace the supplied condition codes with those in your data. trial_query overrides the list of trial_queries and uses selection_label.

With data_path set, the notebook reads that file and compares conditions. With data_path=None, data_paths and data_labels produce one panel per condition comparing datasets—even if the list contains just one file. Labels must correspond to the supplied selections and files.

4 — Resolve input paths, conditions and output settings 
root_path = resolve_project_root(project_root)
print("Project directory:", root_path)

copy_example_inputs(
    ([data_path] if data_path is not None else data_paths)
    + [distance_path or distance_matrix_path],
    base_dir=root_path,
)

output_dir = resolve_project_path(output_dir, root_path)
figure_dir = (
    resolve_project_path(figure_dir, root_path)
    if figure_dir is not None
    else output_dir
)
output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
distance_matrix_path = resolve_project_path(
    distance_path or distance_matrix_path, root_path
)

queries = trial_queries if trial_query is None else [trial_query]
condition_labels = labels if trial_query is None else [selection_label]
input_paths = [data_path] if data_path is not None else data_paths
input_paths = [resolve_project_path(path, root_path) for path in input_paths]
input_labels = [selection_label] if data_path is not None else data_labels
if len(queries) != len(condition_labels) or len(input_paths) != len(input_labels):
    raise ValueError("Supply a label for each input and each condition query.")
5 — Load the supplied response datasets 
datasets = [load_data(str(path), max_subjects=max_subjects) for path in input_paths]
6 — Select observations and report participant counts 
selected_conditions = [
    select_conditions(dataset, queries, complete_lists_only=complete_lists_only)
    for dataset in datasets
]
masks_by_dataset = [[condition.mask for condition in group] for group in selected_conditions]
for dataset_label, group in zip(input_labels, selected_conditions):
    for condition_label, condition in zip(condition_labels, group):
        print(
            f"{dataset_label} / {condition_label}: {condition.trial_count} lists, "
            f"{condition.participant_count} participants"
        )
data, trial_masks = datasets[0], masks_by_dataset[0]

Inspect item alignment

pres_itemids identifies items across lists; it is different from the study-position codes in recalls. You must supply a square numeric distance matrix whose row and column item_id - 1 describe that same global item in every dataset. IDs are nonnegative integers within the matrix’s vocabulary; zero pads unused study slots.

Distances between distinct valid study positions must be finite. Repeated identities at different positions require a finite matrix diagonal entry for that pair. Unused vocabulary entries and a position’s distance to itself may be missing. Choose a distance measure and scale appropriate to your research question; the calculations do not check these requirements.

Use the small item and distance tables below to inspect the mapping. They display a sample; you remain responsible for the full inputs and their scientific item identities.

7 — Load semantic distances or derive them from supplied features 
trial_mask = trial_masks[0]

distance_matrix = jnp.asarray(np.load(distance_matrix_path))
8 — Inspect distances for selected item identities 
matrix = np.asarray(distance_matrix)
row = int(np.flatnonzero(np.asarray(trial_mask))[0])
item_ids = np.asarray(_require_pres_itemids(data))[row].astype(int)
item_ids = item_ids[item_ids > 0][:5]
print(
    tabulate(
        np.column_stack([item_ids, matrix[np.ix_(item_ids - 1, item_ids - 1)]]),
        headers=["Item ID", *item_ids],
        floatfmt=".3f",
    )
)

Inspect one distance rank

The illustration compares a chosen next item’s distance with the alternatives still available. Closer choices receive larger ranks, with midpoint ties. A score of 1 is the closest rank and 0 the farthest; with fewer than two alternatives the score is undefined.

Under uniform choice among available alternatives, the reference is 0.5. This reference concerns ordering according to your matrix, not an independently established measure of semantic organization.

9 — Rank an eligible transition by item distance 
eligible_rows = np.flatnonzero(
    np.asarray(trial_mask) & ((np.asarray(data["recalls"]) > 0).sum(axis=1) >= 2)
)
if not len(eligible_rows):
    print(
        "No eligible transition to illustrate; distance-rank scores are undefined for this selection."
    )
else:
    row = int(eligible_rows[0])
    recall = np.asarray(data["recalls"])[row].astype(int)
    recall = recall[recall > 0]
    previous_position, next_position = recall[:2]
    trial_ids = np.asarray(_require_pres_itemids(data))[row].astype(int)
    previous_id = trial_ids[previous_position - 1]
    next_id = trial_ids[next_position - 1]
    candidates = trial_ids[(trial_ids > 0) & (trial_ids != previous_id)]
    distances = distance_matrix[previous_id - 1, candidates - 1]
    chosen_distance = distance_matrix[previous_id - 1, next_id - 1]
    order = np.argsort(distances)
    print(
        tabulate(
            np.column_stack(
                [
                    candidates[order],
                    np.asarray(distances)[order],
                    (candidates == next_id)[order],
                ]
            ),
            headers=["Candidate item ID", "Distance", "Chosen"],
            floatfmt=".4g",
        )
    )
    print(
        f"Chosen-transition score: {float(percentile_rank(chosen_distance, distances)):.3f}"
    )
  Candidate item ID    Distance    Chosen

Summarize participant ranks

Scores are summarized within participant before calculating the plotted mean and bootstrap interval. The following statistical output tests participant scores against 0.5; it is not a test of the difference between two displayed datasets or conditions. Repeated testing across selections is not automatically multiplicity-adjusted.

Keep the participant CSV for planned follow-up comparisons. Inspect how many finite scores enter each summary: a participant with no eligible transitions cannot contribute an organization score.

10 — Prepare the condition and dataset comparison panels 
panels = comparison_panels(
    datasets, masks_by_dataset, input_labels, condition_labels,
    mode="conditions" if data_path is not None else "datasets",
    selection_label=selection_label,
)
11 — Calculate, plot and save the selected comparison 
fig, axes = plt.subplots(len(panels), 1, figsize=(8, 3.8 * len(panels)), squeeze=False)
for panel_index, (ax, panel) in enumerate(zip(axes.ravel(), panels)):
    panel_data = panel["datasets"]
    panel_masks = panel["trial_masks"]
    curve_labels = panel["labels"]
    title = panel["title"]
    plot_distrank(
        panel_data,
        panel_masks,
        distance_matrix=distance_matrix,
        labels=curve_labels,
        contrast_name=contrast_name,
        color_cycle=color_cycle,
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        bootstrap_method=bootstrap_method,
        n_resamples=n_resamples, bootstrap_seed=bootstrap_seed + panel_index * len(panel_data),
        axis=ax,
    )
    ax.axhline(0.5, color="grey", linestyle="--", label="Uniform-choice reference")
    ax.set_title(title)

    if ax.get_legend_handles_labels()[1]:
        ax.legend(title=contrast_name)
    if ylim is not None:
        ax.set_ylim(ylim[0], ylim[1])
    if yticks is not None:
        ax.set_yticks(yticks)
if figure_str:
    save_figure(str(figure_dir), figure_str, formats=figure_formats, figure=plt.gcf())
else:
    plt.gcf().tight_layout()
plt.show()
12 — Calculate participant ranks and report the existing statistical test 
participant_rows = []
for dataset, dataset_label, condition_masks in zip(
    datasets, input_labels, masks_by_dataset
):
    for condition_label, condition_mask in zip(condition_labels, condition_masks):
        participant_scores = np.asarray(
            subject_distrank(dataset, condition_mask, distance_matrix)
        )
        participant_ids = np.unique(
            np.asarray(dataset["subject"]).ravel()[np.asarray(condition_mask)]
        )
        participant_rows.extend(
            (dataset_label, condition_label, subject, score)
            for subject, score in zip(participant_ids, participant_scores)
        )
        print(
            f"{dataset_label} / {condition_label}: {np.isfinite(participant_scores).sum()} scores; mean {np.nanmean(participant_scores):.3f}"
        )
        print(compare_to_reference(participant_scores, reference=0.5))

13 — Save participant summaries as CSV 
with (output_dir / "participant_ranks.csv").open("w", newline="") as stream:
    writer = csv.writer(stream)
    writer.writerow(["Dataset", "Condition", "Subject", "Rank"])
    writer.writerows(participant_rows)

Retain the uncertainty calculation

The saved summary records the finite participant count, mean, interval and bootstrap settings for each selection. Keep it with the participant-level CSV so that the interval can be interpreted and reproduced.

14a — Save explicit participant-bootstrap summaries 
summary_rows = []
groups = list(dict.fromkeys((row[0], row[1]) for row in participant_rows))
for index, (dataset_label, condition_label) in enumerate(groups):
    values = [
        row[3]
        for row in participant_rows
        if row[:2] == (dataset_label, condition_label)
    ]
    group_seed = (
        bootstrap_seed
        + input_labels.index(dataset_label)
        + len(input_labels) * condition_labels.index(condition_label)
    )
    interval = mean_interval(
        values,
        confidence_level=confidence_level,
        method=bootstrap_method,
        n_resamples=n_resamples,
        seed=group_seed,
    )
    summary_rows.append(
        {"Dataset": dataset_label, "Condition": condition_label, **interval}
    )
with (output_dir / "summary_intervals.csv").open("w", newline="") as stream:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(stream, fieldnames=list(summary_rows[0]))
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(summary_rows)

Reuse the results

The output folder contains participant scores and explicit bootstrap summaries, with the figure and provenance capture. Keep the distance-matrix identity with these results. Pair participant IDs explicitly for follow-up condition comparisons; simulation repetitions are not independent participants.
